Long ago, Murad was a fisherman in a village by the sea. He went out in his boat every morning at dawn and came back before sunset.

Every evening his son Yasin waited for him on a rock by the shore.

One day Murad took his fish to the market in the city across the sea — and did not come back.

Then, days later, the news came: some goods had been stolen from a merchant at the port, and the guards had taken Murad and some other fishermen and locked them up unjustly. They had stolen nothing.

Yasin cried and said to Sheikh Bashir, the imam of the masjid, "My father has never taken anything that belongs to someone else!"

The Sheikh said, "I know that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Free the captive.' Whoever is locked up unjustly is a captive, and freeing him is a right he has over all the Muslims — not only over his own family."

After Jumu'ah prayer, the Sheikh stood up and spoke to the people about the prisoners. He said, "We will send trustworthy men to the judge of the city to tell the truth as witnesses, and we will feed the prisoners' families until they come back."

Then he put a wooden box by the door of the masjid.

People came with whatever they had: one with some coins, another with his ring, another with a goat he had sold at the market.

Then a fisherman who had been out at sea with Murad on the day of the theft stood up and said, "I have no money, but I saw him on his boat with my own eyes. I will go with you and be a witness."

Yasin went to his little box where he had been saving his coins for years, to buy a fishing knife like his father's.

He looked at the coins for a long time. Then he carried all of them to the masjid.

When Sheikh Bashir saw him putting his coins in the box, he said, "Yasin, this is your money."

Yasin said, "And that is my father — and his brothers who are with him."

The trustworthy men sailed to the city, and the witness went with them. They stood before the judge and told him what they had seen. The judge asked questions until he found the real thief, and he ordered the fishermen to be set free.

And every evening Yasin stood on his rock, looking out at the sea.

One evening a white sail appeared far away. As it came closer, Yasin saw his father standing at the front of the ship, waving to him.

Yasin ran along the shore until his clothes were soaking wet.

When the captives came ashore, Murad hugged his son for a long time. Then he walked to the masjid and thanked the people of the village one by one.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Free the captive, feed the hungry, and visit the sick."

📖 Narrated by Al-Bukhari. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
